```{r}
#| eval: false
floraR::flora_search()
```

### Description

Searches a vector of plant names against the locally parsed Flora e Funga do
Brasil (FFB) taxonomic database, returning the best match for each input name
along with its accepted name, taxonomic status, and family. An exact match is
attempted first; if none is found the algorithm falls back to a fuzzy search
within the specified maximum Levenshtein distance.

### Details

The function first attempts an exact match on the `taxonName` column of
the FFB taxon table (a clean binomial constructed from genus, specific
epithet, and infraspecific epithet by `flora_parse`). If no exact
match is found, a generalized Levenshtein distance fuzzy match is performed.
When `genus_fuzzy = FALSE` (default), the genus must match exactly and
only the epithet is fuzzily matched, which is considerably faster for large
lists.

When multiple entries are matched, the one classified as
`"NOME_ACEITO"` (accepted) is preferred.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| splist | A character vector of plant names to search. Each element should include at least a genus and a specific epithet, and optionally an infraspecific rank, infraspecific epithet, and author name. Only valid characters are allowed (see `base::validEnc`). |
| version | Character. FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to `"latest"`. Passed to `flora_download` and `flora_parse`. |
| max_distance | Numeric. Maximum string distance allowed for a fuzzy match, expressed as a generalized Levenshtein distance (insertions, deletions, and substitutions). Can be a positive integer (e.g., `2` allows up to 2 edits) or a fraction of the name length (e.g., `0.1` allows 1 edit per 10 characters). Default is `0.2`. |
| show_correct | Logical. If `TRUE`, a `Correct` column is appended indicating whether the input was exactly matched (`TRUE`) or fuzzily matched (`FALSE`). Default is `FALSE`. |
| genus_fuzzy | Logical. If `TRUE`, the fuzzy algorithm also applies to the genus (slower). If `FALSE` (default), the genus must match exactly and only the epithet is matched fuzzily. |
| progress_bar | Logical. If `TRUE`, a progress bar is printed. Default is `FALSE`. |
| rm_flora_database | Logical. If `TRUE`, the downloaded FFB database folder (`"flora_download"`) is deleted after the search is complete. If `FALSE` (default), the database is kept on disk. Keeping the database is **recommended** because subsequent searches will reuse the existing download, checking if the stored version matches the requested `version`. If the stored version is outdated or different from the requested version, the function automatically re-downloads the correct version. This caching behavior significantly speeds up repeated searches. |
| verbose | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints informative progress messages during parsing and download. If `FALSE`, runs quietly. |

### Value

A data frame with one row per input name and the following columns:

  SearchThe original input name supplied by the user.
  FFB.taxon.IDTaxon ID in the FFB database (`id` column).
  taxonRankTaxonomic rank (e.g., `"ESPECIE"`,
    `"VARIEDADE"`, `"SUBESPECIE"`).
  scientificNameAuthorshipAuthor citation of the matched taxon.
  taxonomicStatusFFB taxonomic status: `"NOME_ACEITO"`
    (accepted), `"SINONIMO"` (synonym), or
    `"NOME_DUVIDOSO"` (doubtful).
  Accepted.taxon.IDID of the accepted name — same as
    `FFB.taxon.ID` when the matched record is itself accepted; the
    parent ID when it is a synonym.
  Accepted.taxon.NameAccepted taxon name resolved from the FFB
    database.
  familyPlant family.
  orderPlant order (when available in the FFB data).
  Correct(Only when `show_correct = TRUE`) Logical indicating
    an exact match (`TRUE`) vs. a fuzzy match (`FALSE`).

Returns `NULL` with a warning if no match is found for any input.
Rows for unmatched names contain `NA` in all FFB columns.

### Examples

```r
# Search a single accepted name (downloads + parses automatically, caches result)
flora_search("Mimosa sensitiva")

# Search with a misspelled epithet; flag fuzzy matches
flora_search("Mimosa sensittiva", max_distance = 0.2, show_correct = TRUE)

# Search a synonym — the result resolves to the accepted name
flora_search("Mimosa pyrenea")

# Search multiple names at once
splist <- c("Mimosa sensitiva", "Swartzia simplex", "Inga edulis")
results <- flora_search(splist, progress_bar = TRUE)

# Use a specific FFB version stored in a custom folder
flora_search(splist, version = "393.418")

# Force fresh download by removing cached database after search
flora_search(splist, rm_flora_database = TRUE)  # Not recommended for repeated use
```
